title: The Distant Colony Again
premise: Rosalind Pemberton smuggles forbidden memories past orbital customs above Meridian, a dying colony the Core worlds abandoned decades ago. When she intercepts a distress signal in a language extinct since the Founding Wars, she discovers a second colony ship, the Halcyon, still adrift with half its cryopods failing — and Meridian's ruling council plans to seize its power core, killing the sleepers to save themselves. Rosalind must choose between her found family among the smugglers and the strangers frozen in the dark. In the end she broadcasts the council's crime to both colonies, wakes the Halcyon's survivors on her own terms, and forges a fragile new settlement where justice is made, not inherited.
about_author: Gideon Voss is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals before turning to fiction. They live off-grid with two cats and an unhealthy interest in dead languages.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Heart
chapters.summary: Rosalind runs a memory-chip shipment through Meridian's corrupt customs, establishing her world: the dying colony, her smuggler crew as found family, and the memories of the old Earth she illegally preserves. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: weary tenderness — she sells other people's pasts because she has no future worth keeping.

chapters.title: The Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Rosalind intercepts a distress call in pre-Founding English and traces it to the lost ship Halcyon, its cryopods failing. The council learns of it too and quietly mobilizes a salvage fleet. Her translator ally decodes a plea: 'We are still people.' POV: Rosalind, with interludes from a waking sleeper. Emotional beat: dread blooming into fierce resolve.

chapters.title: Half of Humanity
chapters.summary: Rosalind infiltrates the council station and discovers their plan: drain the Halcyon's core, letting the sleepers die as 'acceptable loss.' Betrayed by a crewmate who sold them out, she barely escapes with the evidence. POV: Rosalind, then the betrayer's guilt-ridden confession. Emotional beat: the found family fractures under the weight of impossible arithmetic.

chapters.title: What Wakes Us
chapters.summary: Rosalind hijacks the colony's broadcast array, exposing the council's crime to both ships, forcing an open vote instead of a coup. The Halcyon's survivors wake to enemies turned neighbors; the council falls; Rosalind, offered leadership, chooses instead to keep smuggling — now memories of what was done right. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: hard-won belonging, chosen over power.
